sun.upright:
Aries Suns decide with their feet. You're halfway across the room before the question's finished, so a card showing a woman sitting dead still with her eyes covered is about the least Aries picture in the deck. Libra, the card's sign, sits directly opposite Aries. Same axis, other end, you on one side and another person on the other, and that's usually why this card turns up for an Aries Sun. The choice has somebody else's life folded into it, and going first won't settle it.

What you'll notice first is irritation. The Moon is only a visitor in Aries, with no dignity of its own there, and it takes on Mars's colouring, so the feeling under this stalemate runs hot and wants out. Air feeds fire. Every lap of thinking about it winds you up a little more and moves nothing. I've seen plenty of Aries Suns in this spot insist they haven't decided when really they decided weeks ago and are waiting for the other person to make it easy for them.

At work it's the move you'd normally make without asking, the pitch or the resignation, held back because it would land on a team you care about. At home it's the talk with your partner about where you're living, which you keep opening and then shutting again with a joke. Pick whichever one is costing you sleep. Tell the other person which way you're leaning and ask what it would cost them.
sun.reversed:
Turned over on an Aries Sun, this card usually means the waiting has snapped. You've made the call just to end the discomfort of not making it, and the person it affects found out when everyone else did. Mars colouring the Moon likes a clean cut, and it can mistake speed for honesty. The quieter version is just as Aries. You keep charging at everything else, the gym, the side project, a fight with the council, so the one decision that matters never gets its turn.

With a partner it looks like a plan announced over dinner that should have been talked through a month ago. At work it's the email sent at eleven at night. Before you act on anything big, say the decision out loud to the person it lands on and give them a day to answer. You lose very little by waiting a day, and they'll know you asked.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon settles by doing something. You feel it, you act on it, and by the afternoon it's gone, which is healthy in its way and hard work for anyone who likes to talk things through. The Two of Swords sits you down on a cold stone seat and asks you to hold a feeling without acting on it. Its sign, Libra, is opposite Aries, and an opposition often feels like being made to borrow the other end's habits. Here that means thinking about how the other person feels before you've finished feeling it yourself.

It's uncomfortable, and you won't hide that well. The Moon has no rank in Aries. It's a guest there, coloured by Mars, so your emotional reflex is a quick clean reaction, and this card has your arms folded across your chest. Held anger doesn't stay still in you. It leaks. You'll catch yourself snapping about a cup left on the kitchen bench, or driving a bit fast, because the real thing is sitting there unsaid and your body wants a target.

In a share house or a family this looks like keeping the peace with one person and being short with everyone else. Physically it tends to sit in the jaw and shoulders, and sleep goes light. Before you sit down to have the conversation, go for a hard walk or a run to burn off the first heat, and then say the thing in two sentences.
moon.reversed:
Aries Moons don't hold anything for long, and with this card reversed the truce breaks in one hot burst. It all comes out at once, fair or not, and afterwards you feel lighter and the other person feels flattened. Sometimes it goes the other way and the Mars in you turns on yourself. You go flat and restless and can't settle to anything for days, and you can't say why.

Watch for it with a partner or a parent, whoever you've been most careful with, since the blowup tends to land on the person you were protecting. If you've already said it, go back once and give the calmer version with the bit you left out, which is usually that you were hurt. Then leave it alone and let them come to you.

rising.upright:
Aries rising usually walks in first and has said hello before anyone's worked out who you are. With this card the entrance changes, and there's real chart mechanics behind it. With Aries on the Ascendant, Libra falls opposite, on your seventh house, the house of partners and the person across the table. So you've drawn your own seventh house's card for your mask, and you're meeting people the way they usually meet you, weighing it up and holding back.

Mars rules your chart, and the Moon in this card is only a guest in Aries, so the holding back doesn't come naturally and you can feel the effort. Your instinct wants to lead with an opinion. Instead you're saying 'I'm easy' and 'either's fine' and then going home annoyed that nobody guessed what you wanted. Air and fire get on, which helps. Your caution reads as cool and composed, and some people will like you better for it.

In a job interview or a first meeting with a client that works well, since you come across as considered and hard to rattle. On a date, or meeting a partner's friends, it can look like disinterest. Try saying your first instinct out loud once in each new conversation, even something as small as where to eat, and notice how the rest of the conversation loosens.
rising.reversed:
Aries rising can't keep the guarded manner going once the card's turned. You start out careful and then something small tips you, a comment in a meeting, a waiter getting the order wrong, and you come in much harder than the moment deserves. People who'd been reading you as calm get a shock. The other version is a mask that's stuck, polite and closed, while Mars pushes underneath and your face does the talking anyway.

This shows up with new people, a new team, a partner's family, anyone who hasn't seen you at ease. If you've been cool with someone for a while, say one honest thing early in your next conversation with them, before the pressure has time to build. It comes out at a normal volume that way, and the other person can actually hear it.

sun.upright:
Taurus and Libra are both ruled by Venus, and both want life to be pleasant. Taurus wants that in things it can hold, and Libra wants it between people. They're five signs apart, a quincunx, the aspect for a pair that never quite lines up and needs constant small adjusting. So when the Two of Swords lands on a Taurus Sun, the choice is usually a solid one, a house or a job or a sum of money, and the thinking about it has got stuck somewhere above the ground.

Air and earth are opposed elements, talk against proof. You've probably talked about this for months and nothing has physically changed, which a Taurus Sun hates more than almost anything. The part of the card that does suit you is the Moon, which is exalted in Taurus, the Moon at its best, steady and fed and well slept. So your gut is a better instrument here than any list of pros and cons. The trouble is that Taurus stubbornness can pass itself off as balance. I've seen Taurus Suns call a thing undecided for two years when what they meant was that they'd like nothing to change.

With money it's savings sitting still while you weigh the flat against the course. At work it's staying in a role you've outgrown because the other one isn't certain yet. Spend an afternoon doing something physical with the choice. Go and stand in the suburb, sit in the car park of the new office, put the actual numbers on paper in front of you, and notice what your stomach does.
sun.reversed:
When the card's reversed for a Taurus Sun the stalemate has usually set hard. You've stopped weighing it and simply stopped. The job, the relationship, the house you don't love, all left exactly as they are because moving any of it would mean admitting a preference. Taurus would sooner wait out the weather than start an argument. The other form is a sudden lurch after months of sitting still, the car sold in a weekend, the lease signed on impulse.

Money is usually where it shows first, a bill you haven't opened, a subscription you keep meaning to cancel, a loan to a friend you've never mentioned again. In the body it's heaviness, and eating to settle something food can't settle. Pick the smallest piece of the stuck decision and finish it with your hands, the phone call made, the form posted. Do the next piece the week after.

moon.upright:
The Moon is exalted in Taurus. Of all the places it can sit, this is where it's most at ease, and a Taurus Moon usually knows what it needs, a proper meal, a warm bed, the same few people, and settles when it gets them. The Two of Swords brings a Libran Moon into that, a Moon that settles by keeping everyone else comfortable. Those instincts sit five signs apart, the awkward quincunx, and they don't speak to each other easily.

What you'll feel is a body that's steady and a mind that isn't. Your gut is sure. Your head keeps checking whether it's fair to everybody else. There's also a small link through the Six of Pentacles, the Moon's own decan in the middle of Taurus, a card about giving and receiving in fair amounts. So the stuck feeling is often about an imbalance of care. You give more than you get, or you're taking help and feel you owe for it, and you'd sooner sit quietly with that than raise it.

At home it can be the flatmate who never buys the milk, or a parent you're helping with money while your own savings stall. Your partner gets the comfortable evening you won't disturb by saying what's missing. Your sleep will tell you before you admit it, since a Taurus Moon sleeps well when it's settled and badly when it isn't. For a fortnight, jot down what you give and what comes back in one relationship, and don't judge it yet.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, a Taurus Moon holds the feeling so long it turns into comfort-seeking. More toast, another episode, the same route home, anything that feels safe, while the thing you're not deciding sits in the corner of the room. The Moon's exaltation in this sign is a real strength, and upside down it becomes the strength to put up with almost anything for far too long.

It shows up as resentment in the relationship where you give the most and say the least, and as a heavy, clogged tiredness that sleep doesn't touch. It helps to break the stillness with your body before you try to break it with words. Move the furniture, walk a different way to work, cook something you've never made. Then say one true sentence to the person it concerns.

rising.upright:
'Hmm, maybe,' with a pleasant smile, is the answer people keep getting from you. Taurus rising already moves at its own pace, unhurried, solid, a bit hard to budge, and usually people mean that kindly. With the Two of Swords as your mask the calm becomes something they can't read at all. You sit very still, you let them talk, and nobody's sure what you think of them. Venus rules your chart and rules Libra too, so the card's manners come easily to you.

The friction is in the elements. Air and earth are opposed, idea against proof, and Taurus rising trusts what it can see and touch. This card wants you to make up your mind about something you can't see yet. With Taurus on the Ascendant, Libra usually falls on the sixth house, the daily work and the body's routine, so the stalemate is often practical and close in. A role at work, a change of hours, a habit you've been meaning to drop for a year.

Colleagues may find you agreeable and oddly hard to pin to a date. A new friend might take your stillness for coolness and back off before they get to know you. Give people one small clear signal early, a yes or a no to the first thing they ask, and do the long thinking afterwards on your own.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, the Taurus rising stillness becomes a wall. Somebody asks what you'd like and gets nothing, and after a while they stop asking. Or the pressure of not deciding comes out as flat stubbornness about something small, the restaurant, the thermostat, which isn't really the point and everyone in the room can tell.

Because Libra sits on your sixth, it often turns up in the routine. You keep working the same days because changing them means a conversation with a manager, and your neck and shoulders carry the stiffness of it. Have the conversation about hours, or the rota, or the task you've quietly stopped wanting to do. Have it before your case is perfectly ready. A plain first attempt is enough to get things moving.

sun.upright:
Gemini's symbol is a pair, and this is a card about a pair held level, so the fit is almost too good. Libra and Gemini are both air signs, four signs apart, a trine, and trines let things flow without resistance. That sounds lovely and it's also the problem. A card about weighing options, on a Sun sign that finds most options interesting, tends to produce someone who can argue either side of their own life very well and hasn't picked one.

The Moon has no dignity in Gemini. It's a visitor there, picking up Mercury's habits, so the feeling in this card gets turned into talk and analysis almost straight away. You'll have explained this decision to four friends, each time with a slightly different lean, and you may have noticed the story changes depending on who's listening. That's useful. The version you tell the friend you trust most is usually your preference showing.

At work it's two projects run side by side for too long, both stuck at eighty per cent. In love it can be keeping an old flame as a close friend while your partner wonders why. With study it's the course you've enrolled in twice. Write both options on a page, give yourself one minute to circle one, and tell someone which you circled. Listen to how it sounds out loud.
sun.reversed:
The weighing goes into overdrive when this card is reversed on a Gemini Sun. You're reading reviews after midnight, there's a spreadsheet with a column labelled gut feeling, and every new bit of information resets the lot. Air on air, with Mercury colouring the Moon, can spin without end, and it feels like progress because it's busy.

It shows up as a tiredness that starts in the head, as half-written messages in your drafts, and as friends who've stopped asking what you decided because the answer keeps changing. Cut the inputs. Stop researching, mute the group chat on the subject, and pick a date after which the decision gets made on what you already know. Put that date in your calendar and tell one person about it.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon deals with feelings by talking, texting and reading, turning them over in words until they make sense. Put the Two of Swords on that and you get feelings that are beautifully described and not quite felt. The card's Libra trines Gemini and both are air, so there's nothing to slow the thinking down. It runs and runs.

The Moon picks up Mercury's colouring in your sign and has no dignity of its own there, which makes it restless. You can hold two contradictory feelings about a person at once, love and irritation, loyalty and boredom, see both clearly, and still not know what you want. For a Gemini Moon the blindfold is often information itself. Another article, another opinion, another podcast about attachment styles, anything that keeps the actual feeling one step away. I've watched people with this Moon diagnose themselves perfectly and change nothing at all.

With a partner it's the long, clever, circular talk that ends well after midnight with nothing settled. With a sibling or an old friend it's the chat where you keep everyone happy and tell nobody where you stand. It also shows up as a busy mind at bedtime. Put the phone in another room, lie down, and ask which of the two options makes your chest feel lighter. Then leave the question there until morning.
moon.reversed:
A Gemini Moon with this card reversed either floods or goes blank. The flood is every feeling at once, sent as nine messages in a row to whoever's nearest. The blank is a sort of chirpy numbness, where you're funny and quick and busy and haven't really felt anything for a fortnight.

The people closest to you will notice the blank before you do. It shows in sleep, which gets scrappy, and in the way you start three books and finish none of them. Mercury will want to talk it all through. Say the feeling in one short spoken sentence to one person instead. It might be 'I'm sad about Dad' or 'I don't want to move'. Don't add a second sentence explaining it, however much you want to.

rising.upright:
You agree with both people in the argument, and they each go home thinking you're on their side. Gemini rising is usually quick and easy to talk to, the one who asks questions and remembers the answers. With the Two of Swords drawn for your mask you're just as easy to talk to and much harder to pin down. You say 'totally' to the idea and 'fair point' to the objection, and whoever you're talking to walks off charmed and unsure what you actually think.

Mercury rules your chart, and the card's Moon is a guest in Gemini taking Mercury's cues, so your first move is to reach for words. The trine between Libra and Gemini makes the diplomacy smooth. Sometimes too smooth. With Gemini on the Ascendant, Libra falls on the fifth house, romance and play and the things you make, so the careful even-handedness tends to show up where you'd normally be having fun. You're hedging in places where you used to just say yes.

On a date it's plenty of good conversation and no clear signal. In a creative project it's showing everyone two drafts and asking them to choose. Among friends you may have become the one who's neutral about everything, which is restful for them and a bit lonely for you. Pick one small preference, the film, the draft, the person you'd like to see again, and say it first.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, Gemini rising's easy manner starts cracking at the edges. You've agreed with so many people that you've contradicted yourself, and someone's noticed. Or the charm tips into something slippery, telling each side what it wants to hear and quietly hoping they never compare notes. Mercury ruling your chart makes it very easy to talk your way out again, which is exactly the habit to watch.

It often turns up in a friendship group, or around a flirtation kept light for too long. Tidy it up before anyone else does. Go back to the person you were vaguest with and tell them plainly where you stand, in a short message with no jokes in it. It'll probably come out clumsy the first time, and that's fine.

sun.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer. So this card, the Moon passing through Libra, arrives on a Cancer Sun carrying the landlord's key, and it speaks your language. Where it jars is the sign. Libra squares Cancer, both cardinal, both signs that like to start things, and a square forces movement through friction. Cancer's instinct is to protect its own, and Libra's is to be fair to everybody. When the Two of Swords turns up on your Sun, those instincts are usually pulling against each other inside one decision.

It feels like loyalty being weighed and coming up awkward. You want to look after a particular person, you can also see that it isn't fair on someone else, and you'd honestly prefer not to see that. So you fold your arms over it. I've known a lot of Cancer Suns hold a family situation perfectly still for years, never taking a side, because the minute they choose somebody they love gets hurt. There's a faint echo of the Four of Cups too, the Moon's own decan late in Cancer, a card about turning away what's offered. Some of the stillness is that.

It tends to live at home, between a partner and a parent, between two of your kids, or between siblings who aren't speaking. At work it's the colleague you cover for even though they're not pulling their weight. Say to yourself, out loud, who you'd choose if you had to. Then think about what that person needs from you.
sun.reversed:
Upside down on a Cancer Sun, the card tends to mean the family truce has broken and you're standing in the middle holding the pieces. Or you've picked a side at last, loudly, and feel guilty about the other side every hour of the day. The Moon is at home in Cancer, which gives your feelings real weight, and when the balance goes they come out in a rush.

Home is where to look first. The phone call you dread, the family group chat, the relative you're dodging at the supermarket. It also turns up as mothering someone at work so you don't have to think about the people at home. Take one evening completely off from everyone's problems. Then decide what you're willing to carry and what you're handing back.

moon.upright:
You know exactly what you feel, and this card asks you to behave as if you didn't. A Cancer Moon is the Moon in its own sign, the most at home it ever gets, and it feels things fully and keeps them a long time. The Two of Swords borrows that same Moon and sets it down in Libra, where it has no standing and has to mind its manners. So it's like being asked to act as a guest in your own house, keeping a feeling to yourself for the sake of a peace someone else needs.

The square between Libra and Cancer shows up as pressure in the body. Both signs are cardinal and both want to move first, and here neither is allowed to. The feeling gets held behind the ribs, in the stomach, in a tight throat when a certain subject comes up. You usually know what you want. Saying it would upset the arrangement, and for a Cancer Moon the arrangement is the family, the household, the people who lean on you.

It shows up at the dinner table, where everyone's pleasant and nobody mentions it. It shows up in bed, where you lie awake rehearsing the conversation and then don't have it. With an old friend it could be a hurt from years ago you've never raised. Pick one person you trust and tell them the feeling in the plain words you'd use with a child, with no case built and no evidence.
moon.reversed:
With a Cancer Moon, the reversed card means the tide stops being held. Something small sets it off, a forgotten birthday, a tone of voice, and months of feeling come out at the wrong person and at the wrong size. Or the shell closes completely. You go quiet and hurt and wait to see who notices, and most people won't, because they didn't know there was anything to notice.

This lives at home and in the body. Sleep goes, appetite changes, the house gets cleaned very hard. If you've already flooded, apologise for the size and keep the content, because what you felt was real. If you've gone into the shell, send one message to one person saying you're having a rough week, and let them come round.

rising.upright:
With Cancer rising the Moon is your chart ruler, so a card of the Moon drawn for your mask is speaking straight to the planet that steers the whole chart. People already meet you side-on, friendly and careful, checking it's safe before you open up. The Two of Swords turns that up a notch. Arms crossed, face calm, nothing given away.

The square from Libra matters here. With Cancer on the Ascendant, Libra usually sits on your fourth house, home and family and private ground. So the stalemate you're guarding is often a domestic one. What people see is the careful, pleasant version of you, and behind it is a situation at home you're keeping level and not talking about. Air and water are neutral to each other and have to be introduced, and so far your calm face and the home situation haven't met.

At work this makes you seem steady and a touch distant, and colleagues may not realise how much you're carrying. With new friends you might be the good listener who never says anything about yourself. Let one person outside the family know a little of what's going on at home. A few sentences are enough, and your face won't have to do all the work.
rising.reversed:
When the card is reversed for Cancer rising, the careful face slips in public. You're fine through the meeting and then your voice goes at one kind question in the corridor. Or the shell hardens and you come across as prickly, which confuses people who know you as warm. With the Moon ruling your chart, your moods show on you more than you think.

It tends to happen when home and the outside world press into each other, a family problem arriving at work, or a partner turning up at a friend's party halfway through a row. Keep a small buffer. Arrive ten minutes early, sit in the car, and let the feeling finish before you walk in. It's also worth telling one colleague you're dealing with something, so it doesn't come as a surprise.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns like to be seen making the call. There's a generosity in how you decide things, big and warm and public and a bit theatrical, and people generally enjoy it. So a card of someone sitting in the dark with her eyes covered and her hands full is an odd fit for your Sun. It turns up when there's a choice you can't make gracefully, where whichever way you go, somebody will think less of you.

Libra sits two signs from Leo, a sextile, an easy opening that still has to be used, and air feeds fire, so on paper the card should help. It does give you tact and a good sense of how things will look. The Moon is a visitor in Leo, lit by the Sun, and that's where it gets tricky, because your feelings about this want an audience and the card wants them kept level. Pride comes into it as well. Looking unsure is close to unbearable for a Leo Sun, so you'll often present the stalemate as a plan, 'I'm keeping my options open', when really you're stuck.

At work it might be two offers, or a promotion that would mean managing people who've been your mates. In a relationship it's the big gesture you're holding back because you aren't sure it would land the way you want. With your kids, if you have them, it's refusing to take sides out loud while privately having a favourite that day. Tell one trusted person the choice you'd make if nobody could see you making it.
sun.reversed:
The Leo pride takes over when this card reverses. You make a grand decision to get out of the uncomfortable waiting, announce it with confidence, and then you're stuck defending it long after you've privately gone off it. Or you go the other way and refuse to choose at all, and call that being above the whole thing.

Look at work first. The reorganisation you've announced, the project you backed loudly, the stance you took in a meeting that you're no longer sure of. At home it can look like a partner being told what's happening rather than asked. Changing your mind in front of people is hard for a Leo Sun, and here it's the most generous thing you can do. Say 'I've thought about it more and I've changed my mind' to one person who deserves to hear it.

moon.upright:
'Honestly, it's fine,' you say about the dinner nobody told you about, and you mean it for about ten minutes. A Leo Moon needs warmth back. It gives a lot of heart, openly, and feels safe when that heart is noticed and returned. The Two of Swords asks for the opposite of noticing. The feeling goes behind folded arms and stays there, level and quiet, so nobody has to deal with it. For a Moon in fixed fire that's hard, because a feeling in Leo doesn't pass quickly and can sit there for weeks.

The Moon in Leo is a guest in the Sun's house, with no special standing, and it borrows the Sun's need to be seen. Libra's sextile to Leo gives you the manners to hide that well, so you get a very gracious surface over a fairly hurt interior. It's the same with the credit a colleague took, or the friend who's gone quiet on you. I've seen Leo Moons keep up a dignified silence for months because breaking it would mean admitting something mattered.

With a partner it's the hurt you've decided is beneath mentioning. With a close friend it's a loyalty you're quietly weighing, whether to stay close to someone who let you down, and they don't know anything's being weighed. Sleep might come late and restless. Say the hurt once, plainly and warmly, to the person involved, and give them the chance to answer before you've decided what you think of them.
moon.reversed:
When a Leo Moon gets this card reversed, the dignified silence breaks, and it tends to break big. The hurt comes out carrying every week you held it, and it can look like a performance to the other person even though it's completely real to you. The quieter version is sulking, which Leo Moons do very stylishly. Fixed fire keeps a grievance warm for a long time.

It shows up in friendships, especially ones where you're the generous one, and with partners who didn't know they were being tested. The body can run hot, flushed and short-tempered. Pick the person it's really about and tell them, at a normal volume, what you needed and didn't get. Then let them give you something, even if it's small.

rising.upright:
Leo rising tends to fill a room. People notice the hair, the laugh, the way you take the good chair, and they warm to you fast. Drawn for your mask, the Two of Swords tones all that right down. You arrive composed and pleasant and oddly hard to read, with the generous greeting still there and something held back behind it.

Count round from a Leo Ascendant and Libra lands on your third house, the house of everyday talk, messages, siblings and neighbours. So the stalemate you're wearing on your face is often about something you haven't said. There's a text you're not sending, or a conversation with a brother or sister that keeps getting put off. The Sun rules your chart and the Moon has no standing of its own in Leo, which sets wanting to shine against wanting to keep the peace, and the sextile makes it easy to cover the whole thing with charm. People are reading you as gracious. A few of them can tell you're holding something.

At work you'll come across as diplomatic and a good person to chair a meeting, which is useful. With family, especially siblings, you may seem friendly and a long way off. Send the message you've been drafting in your head, the short version, and let the reply be whatever it turns out to be.
rising.reversed:
Once the card is reversed, Leo rising can't keep the composed face up. You're gracious for most of the evening, then one remark lands and you say the unsaid thing loudly, in front of everyone, with a flourish you'll regret on the drive home. Or you go the other way and put on a big bright show so nobody guesses anything's wrong.

With Libra on your third house this usually involves words, a group message, a sibling, a comment under someone's post. Hold off on anything written for a day. When you do say it, say it to the one person, in private, with none of the performance. The drama in you is easy to forgive. It just pulls attention away from what you actually meant.

sun.upright:
Somewhere on your laptop there's probably a document with both options laid out in columns, updated every week, and no decision at the bottom. Virgo Suns want to get it right. You research, compare, read the fine print, and usually end up with the best option because you did the work, so this card is a bit of a trap for you. Libra sits right next door to Virgo, neighbours with little in common, each holding what the other lacks. Virgo wants the correct answer and Libra wants the fair one, and when those point different ways the Two of Swords has you sitting there with one in each hand.

The Moon picks up Mercury's colouring in Virgo, since Mercury rules your sign, and it has no dignity there, so any feeling in the choice gets turned straight into analysis. The elements pull against each other as well. Air is the idea and earth is the proof, and you won't move until the proof is in. With this sort of choice, though, the proof only shows up after you've chosen. So you research a bit more, and then a bit more after that. I see it in a lot of Virgo Suns, and they're usually the most capable people in the room.

At work this is the process you've been asked to fix, with two fair ways of fixing it, while you wait for more data. With your health it's two approaches to the same niggle, and you've read everything about both. Pick a deadline. On that day choose the option that's good enough, and let yourself adjust it later, which is something Virgo is excellent at.
sun.reversed:
With the card upside down on a Virgo Sun, the checking takes over. You redo the comparison, find a flaw in both options, go looking for a third and find a flaw in that. Or you get so tired of it you choose badly and fast, just to stop, and then spend weeks correcting the choice in small ways. Mercury running your sign and colouring the Moon makes that loop very efficient.

It shows up in the body as a tired, tight stomach, and in the diary as tasks shuffled from one day to the next. Hand part of the decision to someone else. Ask a friend or colleague you trust to look over your notes and tell you which one they'd pick, then take their answer seriously for a whole day before you argue with it.

moon.upright:
A Virgo Moon settles when things are in order. A clean kitchen, a list ticked off, a routine that runs, some quiet usefulness to other people. Feelings get handled the same way, by being sorted. The Two of Swords puts a Libran Moon next to that, and because the signs are neighbours with little in common, the card and your Moon don't quite understand each other. Your Moon wants the feeling fixed. The card wants it held level.

Air and earth are at odds, the idea against the thing you can touch, so the held feeling ends up in the body. The stomach, the skin, sleep that starts fine and breaks at three. You'll find yourself reorganising the pantry or answering work email on a Saturday, and it's fairly obviously a way to avoid sitting with the thing you haven't decided. Mercury colours the Moon in your sign, so you can describe the whole situation very precisely. The describing is where it stops.

With a partner it's doing all their small jobs so you don't have to talk about the big one. With a friend it's being extremely helpful about their problems. In your own routine it's a new health kick that's really about control. Once a day, sit for five minutes without a task, let whatever you feel about the undecided thing turn up, and write down one word for it.
moon.reversed:
Turned the other way, this card gives a Virgo Moon a bad case of the worries. The feeling you've been holding level comes out as criticism, of yourself first and then of whoever's nearest, and small things become very important. The dishwasher's been loaded wrong. The email had a typo in it. Or it all turns inward and you feel vaguely unwell for a stretch, tired and fussy about food.

This usually shows at home and around your health. Look for the one undecided thing underneath the fussing, because there nearly always is one. Name it to yourself in a sentence, then take the smallest real step toward it, even a phone call to book something. The fussing tends to quieten once something actual has moved.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising comes across as capable and a bit reserved. Neat, observant, the person who spotted the spelling mistake on the menu. With this card as your mask, people see all of that and also someone who won't commit. You're polite, you've read up, you have a view on both options, and somehow you haven't said which one you'd pick.

Libra is the sign after Virgo, so in most charts with Virgo rising it colours the second house, money, possessions and what you think you're worth. The stalemate showing on your face is often a money one, or a question about your value. Ask for more or wait, charge more or keep the old rate, spend it or save it. Mercury rules your chart and tints the Moon in Virgo, so you'll talk about it in careful, reasonable terms. Air and earth sit awkwardly together, and the careful terms can hide the fact that you haven't worked out what you want to be paid.

In a salary talk or a quote for a client you might come in modest and hedged, which people read as unsure. With new people you can seem helpful and hard to know. Write your number down before the conversation, the actual figure you'd be happy with, and say it first when the moment comes.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the careful Virgo rising manner starts to look anxious. You over-explain, apologise before anyone's objected, add three qualifications to a simple answer. Or the held stalemate turns into nitpicking, and people who meet you get the feeling they're being assessed. A plain yes can end up sounding like a legal document.

The second-house link means money is usually part of it. You're undercharging, or avoiding a bill, or you've been putting off asking for what you're owed, and people tend to take you at the value you set. Send the invoice, ask for the rise, return the thing you bought and didn't want. Do the one money task you've been circling, and do it without a covering paragraph.

sun.upright:
This card is a piece of your own sign. The Two of Swords belongs to the first ten degrees of Libra, the slice the Moon rules, and if you were born in roughly the first ten days of Libra it's your actual decan. Even if you weren't, it's Libra talking to a Libra Sun. Your sign's Major is Justice, a card about weighing things in public and saying the verdict out loud. This is the private end of the same habit, the weighing that goes on alone and never gets announced.

Same element and same sign, so the card amplifies you, for better and for too much. The better part is real. You see how everyone will feel, you're fair, you won't rush anyone. The too-much part is the Libra Sun who won't be the one to decide, because deciding means somebody's disappointed and that somebody might be cross with you. The Moon is a guest in Libra, coloured by Venus, and Venus wants everything to stay lovely. So the stalemate often has a sweetness to it. Everyone's being very nice and nothing is happening.

In a relationship it's the question you and your partner both know is there, the move or the ring or the kids, and neither of you raising it. At work it's being the reasonable one in a dispute between two colleagues for so long that you've become part of the problem. Pick one situation where you've been the neutral party and take a side, kindly, in writing, where you can't quietly walk it back.
sun.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Libra Sun tends to show the cost of too much fairness. You've kept everyone happy for so long that you don't know what you want any more, and when someone asks, the question itself feels like an attack. Or the balance breaks all at once and you make a sharp, uncharacteristic decision, and everyone's surprised to find out you had a temper.

It shows up with partners, where 'I don't mind' has become a habit, and with friends who've learned to decide for you. It can also sit in the body as a tiredness that comes from being pleasant all day. For a week, make three small choices a day without asking anyone, lunch, route, what to watch, and notice that nobody gets hurt.

moon.upright:
The Two of Swords is the Moon in Libra, so with a Libra Moon you've drawn a card of your own Moon's placement, and if your Moon sits in the first ten degrees it's the exact decan too. There isn't much translating to do. You already know this feeling. The need for things to be fair and calm between people, the discomfort when they aren't, the habit of smoothing it over before you've checked whether you actually agree.

The Moon has no dignity in Libra. It's a guest in Venus's house and takes on Venus's wish for everything to stay pleasant, and the same element on the same element makes that louder. With this card drawn the smoothing has gone further than usual, and some part of you has stopped reporting its own feelings because they'd make things awkward. Libra Moons often find out they were upset only when someone else points it out, or when they cry at an advert and can't say why.

At home it's agreeing to the holiday you didn't want, or to Christmas at the in-laws' again. With friends it's being the one everybody tells their side to. Your sleep can go shallow with it, the mind running both people's arguments in a loop. Next time someone asks where you'd like to go or what you'd like to do, answer inside three seconds, before you've checked their face.
moon.reversed:
When this card reverses for a Libra Moon, the peacekeeping usually tips into resentment. You've been fair for months and nobody's been fair back, and it starts coming out sideways, a cool tone, a small cutting remark, a lot of sighing. Or you've gone numb, pleasant with everyone and not really there. Venus colouring the Moon makes it easy to keep the surface lovely while all this builds underneath.

It tends to show with the person you've accommodated most, often a partner or a parent. Tell them one preference you've been swallowing, a small one, and let them deal with it. Their being mildly put out won't hurt you. See how long it lasts, which is usually about an hour.

rising.upright:
Libra rising gives about the most pleasant first impression in the zodiac, and people generally say so. You're easy, well turned out, interested, and you make everyone feel they picked the right seat. This card is a slice of your Ascendant sign, the Moon's ten degrees at the start of Libra, so if you were born with early Libra rising it's sitting right on your Ascendant. Either way it's your own sign's manners, turned up loud.

Venus rules your chart and gives the Moon in Libra its colouring, and air on air amplifies it. So the charm is at full strength, and so is the other side of it, which is that people can't tell what you think. You say something warm to everyone and it's hard to find the opinion in it. I've read for a lot of Libra risings who get told they're lovely and then passed over, because the boss or the date couldn't work out whether they actually wanted it.

In a job interview this looks like a great conversation and no clear ask. On a first date it's a lovely evening and neither of you sure whether it was a date. In a new friendship it can mean months of pleasant coffees. Before the next meeting that matters, decide on one thing you want from it, and say it out loud somewhere in the first ten minutes.
rising.reversed:
Upside down for Libra rising, the charm starts to look like a front. People sense something behind the pleasant face and get a bit wary, or they push to find out what it is. The other form is the pleasantness running out all at once, and a Libra rising who's suddenly curt surprises everyone, you included.

It often shows in first meetings and in roles where you're the face of something, reception, sales, hosting. With Venus ruling your chart the smile comes on by itself, which is why it's worth catching yourself using it. Drop one polite habit for a week, the automatic 'no worries' or the smile when you're annoyed, and say the plainer thing instead. Notice who relaxes around you when you do.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns don't do neutral. You commit fully or you don't come at all, and you usually know what you want long before you say so. So the Two of Swords on your Sun isn't indecision in the usual sense. It's waiting on purpose. Libra is the sign right before Scorpio, a neighbour with little in common, and the card lends your Sun something it doesn't usually have, the patience to hold two outcomes open while you watch.

The Moon is in fall in Scorpio. It's uncomfortable there and unheard, and it has to go the long way round to do its job, which for the Moon is feeling things and letting them show. That fits the card's blindfold more closely than you'd like. You may be telling yourself it's strategy, holding off until you've got all the information, when the feeling is really too big to look at. Scorpio is ruled by Mars, with Pluto added by modern astrologers, so there's a lot of force sitting under the stillness.

In a relationship this is the decision about whether to stay, kept private for a long time while you watch for evidence. With money it's a shared account or an inheritance you haven't brought up. At work it's knowing exactly what you think of the restructure and giving nothing away. Tell one person the real reason you're waiting, and see whether it still sounds like strategy when you say it out loud.
sun.reversed:
For a Scorpio Sun with the card reversed, the waiting ends in a hard cut. You've watched long enough, you've decided, and the other person gets the result without having seen any of the working. It feels clean to you and brutal to them. Or the held position hardens into a stand-off, both of you holding your ground and nobody blinking, for months.

It tends to show up in your closest relationships and anywhere money is shared. With the Moon in fall here, the feeling rarely gets said, so people often have no idea how long you've been hurting. What helps is letting someone see the working. Before the next big move, tell the person affected what you've been weighing and for how long, even if the decision itself stays the same.

moon.upright:
Scorpio is where the Moon falls, the sign where it has the hardest time being heard. A Scorpio Moon feels things at great depth and shows almost none of it, and that's usually been true since childhood. So a card of a woman holding a feeling shut behind crossed arms isn't news to you. You've been doing it for years.

What's different is the reason. A Libran Moon holds still to keep things fair and pleasant, and a Scorpio Moon holds still to stay safe. When both are in play you get someone being very reasonable on the outside while a lot goes on underneath, jealousy maybe, or grief, or a hurt from someone you trusted. Air and water don't clash and don't get on either. They need an introduction, and the polite, weighed-up part of you hasn't properly met the deep part yet.

With a partner it's the thing you've noticed and haven't mentioned, and are watching. With a close friend it might be a betrayal you've decided to be fair about when you're really still angry. Sleep can be heavy and full of dreams. Write down the feeling you're being reasonable about, the actual word, and keep the page somewhere private. That's often enough to loosen it.
moon.reversed:
A Scorpio Moon with this card reversed tends to stop being reasonable all at once. The thing you've been watching gets named, with every piece of evidence you've quietly kept, and the other person is stunned by how long you've known. Or the feeling stays locked down and turns into suspicion, checking phones, reading tone into every message, testing people.

Fall is a hard spot for the Moon, and it makes you slow to trust that your feelings will be heard. This lives in the closest bonds and in how you sleep. Say what you've noticed while it's still small enough to be a question. 'I've felt shut out lately, is something up?' goes a lot further than a file of evidence, and it gives the other person room to be honest too.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising is already hard to read. People meet you and feel watched, kindly or otherwise, and they notice how little you give away in the first half hour. Drawn as your mask, the Two of Swords doubles that. A calm, blank face, a lot of listening, and nothing on show about where you stand.

Libra is the sign just behind a Scorpio Ascendant, which puts it on your twelfth house, the hidden house, the stuff behind the curtain. So the balance this card describes is going on somewhere even you don't look very often. People can sense there's a decision in you, and so can you, dimly, without being able to say what it is. The Moon falls in Scorpio, which makes feelings hard to bring up, and Mars ruling your chart keeps you on guard. None of that is a flaw. It just means a lot happens without witnesses.

At work people may trust your judgement and find you unapproachable. On a date you'll seem intriguing and hard to get close to. Spend some time properly alone somewhere quiet, a long walk, a swim, and let the undecided thing float up without forcing it. Then tell one person what came up.
rising.reversed:
For Scorpio rising the reversed card often means the poker face has started cracking in odd places. You're controlled in the meeting and then you snap at the barista. Or the guardedness gets so complete that people stop trying, and you're left feeling unseen, which isn't what you wanted at all. Mars ruling the chart makes you defend the wall hard, even against people you like.

With Libra tucked into your twelfth house, the thing that's actually bothering you may not be the thing you're reacting to. Sleep can get restless with it. Give yourself an hour alone with no screen and see what's underneath. Then let one person you trust see your face when you aren't managing it.

sun.upright:
Two roads, both still open, and you standing where they split, telling people you're weighing it up. That's this card on a Sagittarius Sun, and for a sign that keeps doors open on principle it's an uncomfortable mirror. You like knowing you could leave, travel, change course, start again, and you've probably arranged your life so most things can be undone. Sooner or later one of these roads closes by itself, and part of you knows it.

Libra and Sagittarius are two signs apart, a sextile, and air feeds fire, so the card doesn't fight your Sun. It encourages it, which is part of the trouble, because every conversation about the choice fires you up about both sides. The Moon is a visitor in Sagittarius, coloured by Jupiter, and Jupiter makes everything look bigger and more possible. There's a link through the Nine of Wands as well, the Moon's decan in the middle of Sagittarius, a card of someone battered and on guard. Some of your hesitation is tiredness. You've taken a big leap before that didn't land, and you remember it.

With travel or study it's the course overseas against staying for the job, or two cities you could live in. In a relationship it's loving someone and loving your freedom and not wanting to say out loud that they pull against each other. Pick a date and write it in the calendar. On that day choose one road and tell three people, so it's harder to wriggle out of.
sun.reversed:
A Sagittarius Sun with this card turned over tends to bolt. You get sick of the fork in the road and just go, a plane ticket, a new job, a dramatic exit, and call it following your gut. Sometimes it is. Sometimes it's the quickest way to avoid feeling the loss of the road you didn't take, and Jupiter colouring the Moon makes the leap feel like an adventure either way. The other version is restless drifting, saying yes to both, the trip and the job, and ending up half in each.

It shows in plans, in money spent on the next thing, and in partners who can't tell whether you're staying. Before you book or sign or quit, ring someone who knows you well and tell them what you're walking away from. Say that part first, before you tell them where you're going.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon feels better with room around it. Space, movement, something to look forward to, a joke when things get heavy. This card asks that Moon to sit still on a stone bench with its arms crossed and go nowhere, which for you is close to torture. Libra is a sextile away and air fans fire, so the card doesn't hurt exactly, and the Libran wish for fairness can make you kinder in a tight spot. It just won't let you leave.

In your sign the Moon takes its colour from Jupiter, which tends to handle feelings by making them philosophical. You turn a hurt into a theory about people. With this card that becomes a way of holding two feelings apart without letting them meet. You're angry and fond, restless and loyal, and you can talk about either one in the abstract for hours. The Moon's decan in Sagittarius is the Nine of Wands, the wary one at the gate, so some of this is self-protection after a knock you haven't quite got over.

In a relationship it's the joke you make every time your partner raises something serious. With family it's the visit you keep moving to another weekend. Your body will want to walk it off, and that genuinely helps, as long as you come back and talk. Next time you feel the urge to change the subject, leave it where it is. Let the silence sit for ten seconds and see what you say next.
moon.reversed:
Turned upside down, the card sends a Sagittarius Moon out the door. You go for a very long drive, book a trip, stay out late with people who don't know about any of it, and you feel wonderful until you get home. Or the restlessness turns inward and goes flat, and the usual optimism disappears for a while. Jupiter's colouring makes escape look like growth, and from the inside it can be hard to tell which is which.

It tends to show with the people who most want you to stay and talk, a partner, a parent, a friend who's been patient. Go on the walk by all means. Take your phone, ring them from halfway round, and say one true thing about how you feel before you get back to the car.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks in open and frank. You ask the direct question, tell the slightly too honest story, laugh loudly, and people feel they know where they stand with you. With this card as your mask, the frankness goes missing. You're friendly and funny and oddly diplomatic, and anyone who knows you well notices you've stopped saying what you think.

Jupiter rules your chart and colours the Moon in your sign, so the instinct is to be expansive. A Sagittarius Ascendant brings Libra round on the eleventh house, friends, groups, the circles you move in and what you hope for, so the careful neutrality on your face is usually about a group. Two friends who've fallen out and both want you on their side. A club or a team splitting over something. You've become the pleasant one in the middle, which is an odd role for a sign that normally says the obvious thing, and the sextile makes you surprisingly good at it.

At a party you'll seem great company and hard to pin down on anything. In the group chat you've gone quiet at exactly the moments people wanted your view. Say what you think in the group, once, as kindly as you can, and let whoever's cross about it be cross.
rising.reversed:
For Sagittarius rising, the reversed card tends to mean the frankness comes back all at once. You've been diplomatic in the group for weeks and then you say exactly what you think at a birthday dinner, and it lands like a dropped tray. Or you quietly leave the group instead, drifting off without explanation because it's easier than choosing a side. Jupiter tends to overdo whatever it does.

Friendships and group settings carry most of this, and the friendship itself is usually fine underneath. If you've blurted, message the person who got the brunt of it and say you meant it more kindly than it came out. If you've drifted, send one message to someone in the group saying why you've been quiet.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns tend to decide slowly and then stick with it for twenty years. You like a plan, a structure, a long view, and you don't mind waiting for the right moment. So on the surface the Two of Swords looks like your kind of patience. It isn't quite. Libra squares Capricorn, both cardinal, both signs that start things, and a square is friction that sooner or later forces a move. The stalemate this card describes is in the way of something you want to build.

The Moon is in detriment in Capricorn, the sign opposite its home, so it works against the grain here and the effort shows. For your Sun that means the feeling side of the decision gets treated as a nuisance, something to manage while you get on with the practical bit. Air and earth are at odds as well, talk against proof, and you want proof. This choice can't be settled on the numbers, though, and part of you knows the numbers came out even months ago. What's left is how you feel, which is the bit you've been careful not to look at.

At work it's the promotion that means moving city, or the business you'd like to start set against the security of the job you've got. With a parent it can be a question about care as they get older, who does what, and you're being very fair and very quiet. Spend one evening writing down how each option would feel in five years, in feeling words, and leave the figures out.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with this card reversed tends either to dig in or to overcorrect. Digging in looks like staying in the stalemate on purpose, calling it discipline, putting the decision off for another financial year. Overcorrecting is a sudden cold call made to end the discomfort, often without telling the people it affects until it's done. Saturn ruling your sign can make either one feel like the responsible thing.

It shows at work first and at home second. A partner may feel they're being managed rather than consulted. Your shoulders will probably tell you before anyone else does. Pick the person most affected by the decision and have a conversation about how it feels for both of you, with no spreadsheet on the table.

moon.upright:
The Moon is in detriment in Capricorn, opposite its home in Cancer, so a Capricorn Moon usually grew up doing feelings the hard way. You cope by being useful, by getting on with it, by having it handled before anyone knew there was a problem. That's admirable, and it's also why the Two of Swords sits so comfortably on you. Holding a feeling level and saying nothing is something you learned very young.

Libra squares Capricorn, so the card and your Moon rub. Libra wants the feeling kept level for everyone's sake. Capricorn wants it kept level because showing it feels weak. With both in play you get someone very composed and quite lonely inside it. The elements don't help. Air against earth is talk against proof, and with this card you'll talk yourself out of the feeling on the grounds that there's no evidence it's justified. A feeling doesn't need evidence to count.

At work it's being the steady one through a restructure while privately you're worried sick. With a parent it might be an old disappointment you've decided it's too late to raise. The body can carry it in the back, the knees, the jaw at night. Tell one person something that's bothering you, and leave out the part about how you're handling it.
moon.reversed:
When the Capricorn Moon's composure goes, it tends to go properly. Months of being fine end in one evening where you're very much not fine, usually over something small, and it frightens you more than anyone. Or it goes the other way, a colder and colder efficiency where you stop feeling much at all and work longer hours to prove it. The square from Libra keeps the pressure building until something gives.

Detriment makes this Moon slow to ask for help. It shows up at work, in sleep that won't come, and in a partner or friend who feels shut out. Let someone see you tired. Book something purely for looking after yourself, a massage, a day off, a long lunch with a friend who makes you laugh, and don't earn it first.

rising.upright:
Nobody in the room could tell you which way you'd vote. That's what this card does to Capricorn rising, which already meets the world composed and a little older than its years. People assume you're competent and they're usually right. With the Two of Swords as your mask you're polite, professional and attentive, and very hard to read.

Capricorn on the Ascendant puts Libra at the top of the chart, on the tenth house of career and public standing, so this card is really about your working life. The stalemate is often a professional one, two paths, two offers, whether to go for the big role. Saturn rules your chart and doesn't hurry, and the Moon is in detriment in your rising sign, so the feeling part of the choice gets pushed out of sight. The square between Libra and Capricorn keeps grinding away underneath, and you're the only one who can feel it.

In a performance review or a pitch you'll come across as measured, which is good, and hard to read, which isn't always. New colleagues may find you distant. In the next conversation with your manager, say one clear sentence about what you want, the actual role or the actual number, and let the rest of the conversation follow from it.
rising.reversed:
For a Capricorn Ascendant the reversed card can mean the professional face gets rigid. You're so careful not to show a preference at work that you come across as cold, or as having nothing to offer, and the opportunity goes to someone louder. Or the stalemate breaks with a sudden resignation letter that surprises everyone, your own family included.

With Libra on your tenth, the career is where to look. Saturn ruling your chart likes to wait until the case is airtight, and this doesn't need an airtight case. Before anything drastic, have one honest conversation with someone senior you trust about what you'd actually like to be doing. It'll feel exposing, which is normal for Capricorn rising.

sun.upright:
Somebody in the group asks what you think, and you give them a very good summary of what everyone else thinks. That's the Two of Swords on an Aquarius Sun. You're good at stepping back far enough that everyone's point makes sense, and people come to you for exactly that. Libra and Aquarius are both air signs, a trine apart, so the card speaks your language fluently and turns it up. Seeing both sides is one of your strengths. With this card drawn it's become a place to stand so you don't have to pick one.

The Moon is a visitor in Aquarius, coloured by Saturn, or by Uranus if you use the modern rulers, and neither is a warm influence. Feelings get held at arm's length and examined. You may have turned the decision into a matter of principle, what's fair, what's right in general, because that's more comfortable than what you personally want. There's a link through the Seven of Swords as well, the Moon's decan late in Aquarius, a card about slipping away quietly with what you need. Sometimes the Aquarius answer to a stalemate is to leave by the side door without telling anyone.

In a group or a cause it's staying neutral in a split you actually have strong views on. In love it's being very reasonable about a partner's request while privately deciding to do nothing. Say the personal version out loud to one person, starting with the word 'I', and keep the principles out of it for once.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the card reversed often goes cold. The detachment that made you fair turns into distance, and people who rely on you feel they're being studied. Or you take the side door the Seven of Swords knows about and change jobs, cities or friendship groups without much warning, with a tidy rationale ready for anyone who asks. Uranus, if you use it, loves a sudden exit.

It shows up in friendships and in how you handle a partner's feelings. Saturn colouring the Moon likes rules and systems, and it can hide behind them very comfortably. Next time someone asks how you feel about something, give them the feeling before the reasoning, even if it comes out untidy.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon feels safest with a bit of space. You like people, often lots of them, and you like being free to think your own thoughts without anyone getting too close to the raw stuff. This card agrees with you rather too well. Its sign trines Aquarius, same element, so there's nothing in it to challenge the distance. It just adds very good manners.

The Moon has no dignity in Aquarius. It's a visitor coloured by Saturn, which likes things controlled, or by Uranus, which likes them unusual, and either way feelings get sent upstairs to be thought about. With this card the thinking has become the whole of it. You can explain very clearly how you feel about the situation without quite feeling it. Aquarius Moons often find the feeling turns up later, days later, in a supermarket queue, for no obvious reason.

With a partner it's agreeing calmly to something that needed a proper conversation. With friends it's being everybody's sensible friend and nobody's close one for a while. Sleep might be fine while the dreams are anything but. When you notice you're explaining a feeling, stop halfway through the sentence and say the one word that describes it.
moon.reversed:
Turned round for an Aquarius Moon, the card shows the distance becoming a wall. You stop answering messages. You say you're fine in a tone that clearly means leave me alone. Or, less often, the feelings you kept upstairs come down in a rush, and you're startled by how much there was. To people who don't know you well it can look like coldness.

It shows in friendships most, and with anyone who's tried to get close. Saturn in the background makes you proud of coping alone, and the Seven of Swords foothold in your sign makes the quiet exit tempting. Pick one friend and tell them you've been keeping your distance and why, even if the why is only a guess. They'll probably have noticed already.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising comes across as friendly and a little unusual. You'll talk to anyone, you've got odd interests, and there's a cool edge people either like or find hard to get past. With this card drawn for your mask, the cool edge wins. People find you pleasant, fair, interested in their ideas and completely noncommittal about your own.

For Aquarius rising, Libra is the ninth-house sign, the house of beliefs, study, travel and the long view, so the stalemate on your face is often about what you believe or where you're headed. A course you might take. A move overseas. A faith or a politics you've drifted from without saying so. The trine between the signs makes it easy to discuss all of it very calmly, and air on air means you could keep discussing it for years. Saturn rules your chart, with Uranus too if you use the modern rulers, and between them you get someone who looks settled and is quietly planning a change.

At a dinner you'll be the one who sees merit in everyone's argument. With a mentor or teacher you might stay polite and keep your real question back. Write down the belief or plan you've been sitting on and give it one concrete step, an enquiry sent, a brochure ordered, a conversation booked.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising with the card reversed can look aloof, or contrary. You take the opposite view in any discussion so nobody can pin you to your real one, and people find that tiring after a while. Or the change you've been quietly planning happens abruptly, the ticket booked, the course enrolled in, and the people around you hear about it last. Uranus, if you use it, enjoys the surprise far too much.

With Libra on the ninth, it's often a belief or a big plan. A friend who's sure you'd never leave may be the last to know, and hurt by it. Tell the people it affects before you act, even briefly, and let them ask a question or two before it's settled.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns feel their way through a decision. You pick up what everyone involved wants, often before they've said it, and you can feel both options from the inside. So when this card turns up on your Sun, the trouble is usually that you know too many people's feelings at once and can't find your own among them. Libra weighs and Pisces soaks things up, and the two signs sit five apart, a quincunx, with nothing in common and a lot of constant adjusting to do.

The Moon is only a guest in Pisces, coloured by Jupiter, or Neptune in modern terms, and both of those widen things out. Your feelings don't have edges. That's lovely in some parts of life and very hard in a choice, because this card needs you to draw a line somewhere. Air and water are neutral to each other, so the clean Libran weighing and your tidal way of feeling need introducing, and so far they haven't been. Pisces' own Major is The Moon, a card about fog and half-seen things, and there's some of that here too.

At work it's two roles, or a creative project against a steady job, and you're waiting to feel sure. In a relationship it's staying because leaving would hurt them, until that's hard to tell apart from wanting to stay. Sit somewhere quiet and imagine telling each person your decision, one after the other, and notice which conversation lets you breathe out.
sun.reversed:
Pisces Suns with this card reversed tend to drift. You don't decide, you let the choice slip past until circumstances decide for you, and then you tell yourself it was meant to be. Sometimes that's fine. Other times it leaves you living a life somebody else picked. The other form is overwhelm, when all the feelings you've been holding for everyone else flood in at once.

It shows up in work that stalls, in plans that fade, and in a tiredness that sleep doesn't clear. Jupiter and Neptune both like to make things bigger and blurrier. A quincunx always asks for small adjustments, and this is a moment to make one. Shrink the choice to the very next step and take only that, then ask someone steady to check in with you in a few days.

moon.upright:
The woman on this card sits with her back to the water, which is about the least Pisces thing a person can do. A Pisces Moon soaks up the mood of whatever room it's in. You feel other people's sadness in your own chest, you cry at the news, you need time alone to wring yourself out. This card asks that Moon to hold a feeling shut and level, and you aren't built for shutting. Libra and Pisces sit a quincunx apart, awkward at a distance, always adjusting.

Jupiter, and Neptune for modern astrologers, colour the Moon in your sign, and neither gives it edges. So when you try to do what this card does and hold a feeling still, it leaks into everything else. You're not sad about the decision exactly. You're sad in general, tired, dreamy, a bit lost, and it takes a while to trace it back. Air and water have to be deliberately introduced, which here means putting a feeling into plain words so you can look at it.

With a partner it's absorbing their mood and losing track of yours. With family it's the relative whose problems you carry round. Sleep can be long and not very restful, and water helps, a bath, a swim, a walk on the beach. Afterwards, while you're still calm, write one plain sentence about what you want, and read it again the next morning.
moon.reversed:
When a Pisces Moon has the card reversed, the held feeling tends to come out as a flood. Tears that seem to arrive from nowhere, a sudden need to be alone, a day in bed. Or you escape it, into screens, long sleeps, someone else's drama, anything that means you don't have to feel your own. Neptune, if you use it, makes the escape hatch very easy to find.

This tends to show in sleep and in your closest relationship. Be gentle with the flood and a bit firm with the escaping. Pick one of the escapes and cut it back for a week, and in the space it leaves, tell one person what's actually going on with you.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets people softly. You're warm, a bit dreamy, easy to talk to, and people tend to tell you things within ten minutes of meeting you. With the Two of Swords as your mask that softness gets a fence around it. You're still kind and still listening, and you've gone vague about yourself in a way people notice.

In most charts Pisces rising has Libra on the eighth house, shared money, intimacy, debts, inheritances, whatever gets merged with another person. So the careful balance you're keeping on the surface is often about something private and shared. A joint account. How close to let someone get. Money owed to or by family. Jupiter rules your chart and Neptune co-rules it for modern astrologers, both of them blur things, and the quincunx between Libra and Pisces makes the clean line this card wants hard to hold.

On a date it can come across as mysterious, which is fine until you realise you haven't said anything true about yourself all evening. In a money conversation with a partner or a relative you'll agree to things to keep it pleasant. Before the next talk about shared money, write down the one thing you need out of it and take the paper with you.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising with the card reversed can slip right out of focus. People find you hard to reach, messages go unanswered, plans get cancelled with a vague apology. Or the fence comes down all at once, and you tell a near-stranger at a party far too much and feel exposed for days afterwards. Both leave people unsure where they are with you.

With Libra on your eighth, it often circles shared money or closeness, a partner, a sibling, a friend who owes you. Neptune co-ruling your chart makes vagueness feel like kindness. Be clear about one boundary, in words, with the person it concerns. 'I can't lend that' or 'I need to go slower' is enough. Say it once and then stop explaining.

1.upright:
The first house is the body and the way you start things, how you walk into a room and what you do in the first minute. It's Aries' natural house, ruled by Mars, and Libra is the sign directly opposite. So a Libran card here is the far end of the axis turning up at your front door. The part of the chart that's meant to be about you acting on your own behalf has filled up with other people's opinions about what you should do.

It's an angular house, one of the corners of the chart, and what happens there is visible. People can see you hesitating. Air feeds fire, so the card isn't hostile to the house, and it can make you more thoughtful at the start of things than you usually are. The strain is that the first house needs a direction and this card offers two. You may notice it physically, arms folded more than usual, a slight stoop, a habit of starting every sentence with 'I don't know'.

Look at how you're beginning things. A new job where you haven't yet said what you'd change. A style you keep meaning to try. A fitness plan you keep adjusting before you've started it. Even your clothes can go safe and neutral and a bit invisible. Make one change to how you present yourself that's purely your own preference, and don't ask anyone's opinion on it first.
1.reversed:
A long stall in the first house often ends, with the card reversed, in a lurch. You make a big personal change fast, a new look, a new gym, a move, partly to prove you can still decide something. Mars as the house's natural ruler rather likes that. The other form goes the opposite way, so worn down by everyone's input that you stop presenting much of a self at all, and people start describing you as 'fine'.

The first house is the body, so that's the place to watch. Tight shoulders, a clenched jaw, a tiredness that isn't about sleep. Pick one small physical thing you've been putting off for yourself, a haircut, a check-up, a new pair of shoes, and book it without consulting anyone.

2.upright:
Money and what you think you're worth. The second house is real money, the account balance, the rent, the price you put on your time, and it's Taurus's house, which is where the Moon is exalted. So the card's planet is welcome here. The Moon does well around solid things, food and savings and a secure roof, and it brings good instincts to money when you let it. The sign is the awkward part. Libra and Taurus are a quincunx apart, never quite aligned, and air against earth is talk against proof.

From the inside that looks like a financial decision that's been talked about far more than it's been acted on. Two ways to spend a lump sum. Whether to ask for a rise. Whether to lend money to a friend or keep it. You may feel it has to be fair to everyone, and the fairness question has turned into a way of not noticing what you actually value. Venus rules both Libra and Taurus, so pleasure and comfort are in this too, and so is guilt about wanting them.

The banking app you open and close without looking properly is the usual giveaway, along with the invoice you haven't sent because the amount feels awkward. With a partner it might be the unspoken question of who pays for what. Sit down with the real numbers for half an hour, write down the option your gut prefers, and act on one small piece of it before you lose your nerve.
2.reversed:
The money stalemate can harden into plain avoidance when this card is reversed in the second house. Bills stack up unopened, a savings plan stalls, or a sum you're owed goes unasked for because asking would be awkward. The other extreme is a sudden spend or a sudden cut, made in one go to end the tension of not deciding. Worth is in this too, and undercharging for your work is a common form of it.

The Moon's exaltation in Taurus means your instinct about money is usually sound, so the problem is rarely judgement. It's looking. Open the account, the letter, the statement, and read the actual number. Then make a single decision about it, a small one, and write down what you decided and why.

3.upright:
The Moon has its joy in the third house. Of all twelve, this is the one where the old astrologers said it did its best work, among everyday talk, siblings, neighbours, short trips, the messages going back and forth all day. So the card's planet is happy here, and the sign is too. Libra trines Gemini, the house's natural sign, both air, so the Two of Swords speaks the house's own language. It's one of the easier places for the card to land, and also one where it can talk itself in circles.

What's live is a conversation you're managing very carefully. You're fair, you're measured, you can see how both people will take it, and the words are good. Air in an air house amplifies that, and it can tip into saying a great deal while committing to nothing. With siblings especially, you may be keeping the peace by being the one who never takes a side. With a neighbour it could be a small dispute you're being extremely reasonable about. I often see this placement in someone who's rewritten the same text four times.

Your drafts folder is probably full. There's likely a sibling group chat where you've gone very diplomatic, a course you're halfway through choosing, and a visit to a relative that keeps getting moved. Take one of those careful messages, cut it to three sentences, and send it.
3.reversed:
In the third house the reversed card turns careful talk into either silence or blurting. You stop replying to a sibling, leave a message on read for weeks, avoid the neighbour in the street. Or the measured tone snaps and you send the unedited version at midnight to the family chat, and then wish you hadn't.

Because the Moon rejoices in this house, feelings tend to come out through words here, for better or worse. If you've gone silent, send a short message saying you've been quiet and you're still around. If you've blurted, follow up once with the calmer version and leave it at that. A phone call often works better than more text.

4.upright:
Everyone at home is being very reasonable, and nobody's saying what they need. The fourth house is the Moon's own house by nature, Cancer's territory, so this card is on home turf here in the most literal way. It's home and family, the kitchen table, the parents you came from and whoever you share a roof with. The Moon knows this ground. What it carries in from Libra is harder, because Libra squares Cancer, and the square is friction that eventually forces something to move.

Inside a household that feels like fairness getting in the way of closeness. Who does the dishes, whose family you visit, who gets the bigger room, who looks after Mum. Air and water don't naturally mix, and the tidy weighing-up of a Libran Moon sits oddly against the feelings a home is actually full of. It's an angular house, so none of this stays hidden for long. The people you live with can feel the truce even if nobody names it.
